chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Salih ibn al-Sindi from Ja'far ibn Bashir from Isma'il ibn Muhammad al-Khuza'i, who said:

Abu Baseer asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while I was listening, saying: 'Do you think I will live to see the Qa'im (the Awaited One)?' He said: 'O Abu Baseer, do you not know your Imam?' He said: 'Yes, by Allah, and it is you.' And he took his hand. He said: 'By Allah, O Abu Baseer, you should not mind if you are sitting with your sword in the shadow of the Qa'im's tent.'

key_terms.إِمَامَكَ: Your Imam, referring to the specific Imam of the era
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Awaited One (al-Qa'im), referring to Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَوَاق: Tent or pavilion, often used metaphorically for the camp or presence of the Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Abu Baseer witnessing the Qa'im?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reassures Abu Baseer of his imminent death during the era of the Awaited One (al-Qa'im), using the metaphor of sitting with a sword in his shadow to signify active readiness and honor. This highlights the Shia concept of *Intizar* (expectation) not as passive waiting, but as a state of preparedness for the Imam's appearance, affirming the continuity of spiritual authority through the Ahl al-Bayt.
